The `solVuDuDessous` lever instead keeps the LOWEST one, but it was capped at 4 m below play level, a margin written to "cover stairs and dips WITHOUT letting a basement show through": the guardrail forbade exactly what was being asked for. Set to 6 m to save elevated structures, it changed NOTHING on Vagabond, Command, and High Ground — so the surfaces the substitution flattens there are all beyond 6 m — and on Snowbound it brought BACK THE MUSH, which was the announced risk. What the measurement establishes: on these maps, weakening the substitution doesn't render the structures, it renders the shells. This is a tradeoff, not a setting to be found — missing structures and mush are two faces of the same lever. REFERENCE TAKEN ON THE NAVMESH'S TOP LEVEL, on 2026-08-30, second attempt at the missing floors. The first attempt — removing the ground tolerance — changed nothing, and that is what pointed to the real cause: it isn't an erasure that removes the floors, it's the SUBSTITUTION. Wherever the map is judged covered, `substitueParReference` replaces the drawn surface with the one closest to the reference; but the reference drawn from the navmesh kept, wherever two levels overlap, THE LOWEST ONE. A floor, a walkway, a bridge were therefore flattened onto the ground below — by construction, not by accident. Taking the HIGH level, they survive. And the roofs don't come back either: a roof isn't in the navigation mesh, you don't walk on it. The navmesh only contains walkable surface, so its highest level is the last floor where someone's feet can land. WHAT THIS COSTS: wherever a walkway crosses over a courtyard, you see the walkway and no longer the courtyard. That's the normal choice of a top-down view. GROUND TOLERANCE REMOVED on 2026-08-30: the user reports MISSING STRUCTURES on this map — "bridges or floors."
